summary:
Rootwise is a location-aware agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers make informed crop selection decisions using Earth observation data and environmental intelligence.
Our project combines a crop recommendation engine, a geospatial environmental data pipeline, and a FastAPI backend into one integrated system. We processed 2,380 geographic grid cells covering Bengaluru Urban, incorporating satellite-derived and environmental indicators such as rainfall, temperature, humidity, soil moisture, vegetation health (NDVI), and evapotranspiration.
When a farm is registered, Rootwise identifies its corresponding geographic grid cell, retrieves available environmental observations, and generates three ranked crop strategies based on farm characteristics and available inputs.
Our recommendation engine also supports climate-sensitive water-use scoring, demonstrated through controlled rainfall scenarios.
Rootwise aims to make environmental information more accessible and actionable for agriculture, supporting better planning, resource awareness, and more sustainable farming practices. Future development will integrate recent seasonal datasets for operational climate-adjusted recommendations.
details:
Rootwise — Project Details

Problem Statement

Agricultural planning depends on several environmental factors, including rainfall, soil conditions, water availability, temperature, and vegetation health. However, these datasets are often scattered across different platforms and are difficult to interpret for practical crop selection.

Farmers need accessible tools that connect geographic and environmental information with actionable agricultural recommendations.

Our Solution

Rootwise is a geospatial agricultural decision-support prototype that integrates Earth observation data with a crop recommendation engine.

The system connects three main components:

1. Crop Recommendation Engine

Our Python-based recommendation engine evaluates farm characteristics such as soil type, irrigation availability, and location. It generates three ranked crop strategies, supported by scoring evidence and explanations.

The engine also supports seasonal climate-sensitive water-use scoring when suitable rainfall, irrigation, and crop water requirement inputs are available.

2. Environmental Data Pipeline

Our environmental pipeline processes geographic and environmental observations for Bengaluru Urban.

The prototype dataset includes:

  • 2,380 geographic grid cells
  • Rainfall
  • Minimum and maximum temperature
  • Humidity
  • Soil moisture
  • Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI)
  • Evapotranspiration

The dataset contains historical observations dated January 1, 2016. Missing measurements are preserved rather than replaced with misleading values.

3. Backend and Database

We developed a FastAPI backend connected to PostgreSQL for storing farms, geographic regions, map cells, and environmental observations.

When a farm is registered, Rootwise uses its geographic coordinates to identify the matching grid cell and retrieve available environmental observations.

The backend integrates the recommendation engine and returns ranked crop strategies through REST API endpoints.

Technical Architecture

Farm Registration → Geographic Coordinate Matching → Environmental Data Retrieval → Recommendation Engine → Ranked Crop Strategies

Technologies Used

  • Python — recommendation engine, data processing and backend services
  • FastAPI — REST API development
  • PostgreSQL — structured data storage
  • PostGIS — geospatial database support
  • SQLAlchemy and Alembic — database models and migrations
  • Docker — local database environment
  • GeoJSON and JSON — geographic and environmental data exchange
  • Pytest — automated testing
  • Git and GitHub — version control and collaboration

Innovation

Rootwise combines environmental data ingestion, geographic farm matching, and explainable crop recommendation scoring within a modular architecture.

Rather than providing only generic crop suggestions, the system is designed to connect recommendations to specific farm locations and available environmental evidence.

The scoring engine can respond to changing seasonal conditions. In controlled synthetic tests, the water-use scores for cowpea, groundnut, and green gram increased from 25 to 100 when rainfall inputs increased.

Validation and Results

Our integrated prototype successfully:

  • Ingested 2,380 geographic grid cells and 2,380 environmental observation records
  • Matched a test farm to its geographic grid cell
  • Retrieved corresponding historical environmental observations
  • Generated three ranked crop strategies
  • Demonstrated climate-sensitive scoring using controlled test scenarios
  • Passed 51 automated tests across the engine and backend

Expected Impact

Rootwise aims to support informed agricultural planning, improved awareness of environmental conditions, and more sustainable use of water and land resources.

The system is designed to be extensible to additional geographic regions, datasets, and agricultural decision-support features.

Current Limitations and Future Development

The current environmental dataset represents a historical observation date rather than live seasonal conditions.

Future development will focus on integrating recent seasonal observations, validating crop recommendations against agricultural evidence, improving geospatial query performance, and providing an accessible farmer-facing interface.

Rootwise is a working technical prototype, not yet a validated operational farming advisory service.
